national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi today released the autobiography of former President Ram Nath Kovind, titled ‘Triumph of the Indian Republic: My Life, My Struggles’ in New Delhi. The autobiography offers a deeply personal account of Mr Kovind’s remarkable life journey, tracing his experiences, struggles and achievements from his early years to his distinguished public life and eventual service as the 14th President of India. The book provides insights into the values, experiences and circumstances that shaped his journey and public service. Speaking on the occasion, Mr Modi said that Ram Nath Kovind’s guidance as the President has been a great source of strength for him. He said that Mr Kovind’s autobiography will not only provide insights into his life, personality, and contributions but also serve as a legacy for Indian democracy and society. Prime Minister Modi said that even after retiring from the country’s highest constitutional office, Ram Nath Kovind has remained actively engaged and continues to work on important issues such as One Nation, One Election. Prime Minister Modi urged the younger generation to learn about Ram Nath Kovind’s life journey in his own words and read about his writings and experiences. He said, great personalities such as Mahatma Gandhi, Babasaheb Ambedkar, Jyotiba Phule and Savitribai Phule dreamed of rebuilding India, an India where even the poorest and most deprived would have the opportunity to reach the highest positions. Mr Modi said that personalities like Ram Nath Kovind, through their hard work and capabilities, have not only transformed their own lives but have also played a significant role in turning those centuries-old dreams and visions into reality. On the occasion, Ram Nath Kovind said that politics is not merely a means of acquiring power, but an instrument of serving the nation. He said, education opens the doors to countless possibilities and provides new directions and innumerable opportunities in life. Mr Kovind said that today, under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana, crores of people have been provided with a roof over their heads.

national_raw_news.title: 3 hours ago | National 137 HM Amit Shah to move Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026 for consideration and passing in Rajy...
national_raw_news.content: Union Home Minister Amit Shah is scheduled to move the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026 for consideration and passing in Rajya Sabha today to alter the name of Kerala. In Lok Sabha, Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 to be tabled for consideration and passing. The Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill seeks to change the name of the state of Kerala to Keralam in the First Schedule of the Constitution. A resolution in this regard was passed by the Kerala Legislative Assembly in June 2024. The resolution stated that while the State is known as Keralam in Malayalam, its name is recorded as Kerala in the First Schedule of the Constitution. Meanwhile, the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill 2026 aims to amend the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957. The bill aims to make India’s mining sector more efficient, investment-friendly and well equipped to fulfill the country’s growing demand for critical minerals.

national_raw_news.title: 3 hours ago | National 84 IMD forecasts heavy rainfall over several parts of the country for next two to three days
national_raw_news.content: The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued orange alert for heavy to very heavy rainfall over East Rajasthan, Madhya Maharashtra, Odisha, Jharkhand and Gangetic West Bengal today. The Met department has predicted heavy rainfall over North eastern parts of country, Sikkim, Sub Himalayan West Bengal, Chhattisgarh, West Madhya Pradesh, West Rajasthan, Gujarat, Konkan, Goa, Punjab, Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir along with and Andaman and Nicobar Islands for the next two three days. According to IMD, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan are likely to experience thunderstorm accompanied with lightning and gusty winds till tomorrow. Similar conditions are expected to prevail over Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, and Uttarakhand till Saturday.

national_raw_news.title: 3 hours ago | National 83 Supreme Court asks 19 States and UTs to consider declaring cancer a notifiable disease
national_raw_news.content: The Supreme Court has asked the 19 remaining States and Union Territories to consider declaring cancer a “notifiable disease” to facilitate early detection and ensure proper care of patients. A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, issued the direction yesterday. The court was informed that 17 of the 36 States and Union Territories have already notified cancer as a notifiable disease, following recommendations made by a Parliamentary Standing Committee. The Supreme Court had earlier issued notices to the Centre and all States and Union Territories on a Public Interest Litigation-PIL seeking a direction to declare cancer a notifiable disease across the country. The Centre told the court that health is a State subject and pointed out that 17 States have already notified cancer. The court directed the remaining States and Union Territories to consider the recommendations and take appropriate decisions. It also directed them to file compliance affidavits. The Supreme Court has also sought measures for implementing cancer screening across the country.

national_raw_news.title: 3 hours ago | Sports 105 Indian fencers win two gold, three silver and four bronze medals at Commonwealth Championship
national_raw_news.content: India continued its impressive medal-winning run at the Commonwealth Fencing Championship in Lagos, Nigeria. After securing 17 medals on the opening day on Monday, Indian fencers added more Medals to the country’s tally. Karan Singh and Sherjin Shanthimol clinched gold medals for India in the senior men’s events last night. In the men’s Sabre final, Karan Singh staged a remarkable comeback against Australia’s Yoongi Shim. Trailing 7-11, Karan fought back strongly to win the bout 15-12 and claim the gold medal. In the men’s Epee final, Sherjin Shanthimol defeated second-seeded South African fencer Pieter Kruger 15-6 in a comfortable victory to secure the top spot. India also won a bronze medal in the senior men’s Foil event, with Tejas Patil finishing on the podium in a field featuring several renowned international fencers. Indian women fencers put up another dominant performance in the senior women’s Epee event, winning three medals. Tanishka Khatri clinched the gold, while her compatriot Khushi Dabhade took the silver. Prachi Lohan added a bronze medal to India’s tally, sharing the third position with Australia’s Harrison Asley. In the individual Sabre event, Indian women won three medals. Aakhari secured the silver medal, finishing behind England’s Brierley, while Shruti Joshi and Jefarlin won bronze medals.

national_raw_news.title: Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav reaffirms India’s commitment to elephant conservation on World Elephant Day
national_raw_news.content: On World Elephant Day, Minister of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Bhupender Yadav, today reaffirmed India’s commitment to securing a shared future for elephants and people. In a social media post, Mr Yadav highlighted that with 33 Elephant Reserves across 14 States, 150 scientifically validated elephant corridors, advanced population monitoring and stronger measures to mitigate human-elephant conflict, India continues to strengthen elephant conservation. He said that when the future of elephants is secure, the forests, biodiversity and ecological heritage are also secured. The Minister urged the citizens to ensure that the elephant continues to walk freely through India’s forests and landscapes for generations to come.

national_raw_news.title: Rail Coach Factory Kapurthala rolls out first rake of 19 LHB coaches for Bangladesh Railways
national_raw_news.content: The Rail Coach Factory, Kapurthala, in Punjab, is rolling out the first rake comprising 19 LHB broad gauge passenger coaches for Bangladesh Railways today. The rake comprises 03 AC Sleeper Cars, 03 AC Chair Cars, 11 Non-AC Chair Cars and 02 Power Cars. These coaches incorporate several unique design features and modifications, many of which have been developed for the first time in such type of coaches. The coaches have been specially customised to meet the operational and passenger requirements of Bangladesh Railway. The seating arrangement incorporates specially designed reclining chairs with stainless steel armrests and stainless-steel footrests, offering multiple reclining positions for enhanced passenger comfort. They also have an integrated CCTV surveillance system, a passenger alarm system, a Baby Care Room and a Prayer Room. The association between RCF, Kapurthala and Bangladesh Railway began with the successful supply of 120 LHB broad gauge passenger coaches during 2015-16.

national_raw_news.title: Dr Bhooma VG selected for Vice-Chancellor post at Atal Bihari Vajpayee Institute in Mauritius: MEA
national_raw_news.content: Ministry of External Affairs today informed that Dr Bhooma VG (IRPS (Retd)) has been selected for the post of Vice-Chancellor at the Atal Bihari Vajpayee Institute of Public Service and Innovation (AIPSI) of Mauritius. In a statement, the Ministry said that AIPSI, the erstwhile Civil Service College of Mauritius, was jointly inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the Prime Minister of Mauritius, Navinchandra Ramgoolam, in March 2025. It added that the Institute is being developed as a premier training agency and a centre of excellence for the African region and will become an awarding body. The Ministry further informed that Dr Bhooma is expected to take up her assignment shortly.

national_raw_news.title: British Deputy High Commissioner and Punjab NRI Affairs Minister discuss issues concerning Punjabi diaspora in UK
national_raw_news.content: The British Deputy High Commissioner, Alba Smeriglio, discussed various concerns of Punjabis residing in the United Kingdom, including the issues affecting their interests. Both Ms Smeriglio and Punjab’s NRI Affairs Minister Dr Ravjot Singh, during their meeting yesterday at Chandigarh, emphasised the need to further strengthen mutual communication and cooperation on matters concerning the Punjabi diaspora. The Deputy High Commissioner also visited a village in Ludhiana to educate the youth about visa fraud and safe and legal mobility to the UK. Later, taking to her official social media account, she said she had a great opportunity to connect directly with people and listen to their experiences. She said access to accurate information is one of the best ways to protect people from visa fraud and unsafe migration routes.

national_raw_news.title: India wins 17 medals, including 4 gold, on opening day of U-23 Commonwealth Fencing Championship 11 Aug 2026 | 7:55 AM 646
national_raw_news.content: India has made a strong start at the U-23 Commonwealth Fencing Championship in Lagos, Nigeria, winning 17 medals, including 4 gold, on the opening day. The Indian contingent has secured 4 gold, 4 silver and 9 bronze medals at the championship, which began on Sunday. Indian fencers reached the podium in all 6 individual events across the Sabre, Foil and Epee disciplines. In the men’s Sabre event, Nikhil Wagh won the gold medal, while Lakshay Badser secured silver. Ashwini Arya and Laishram Moramba bagged bronze medals. In men’s Foil, Tejas Patil won silver and Hemash Sanasam secured bronze. In men’s Epee, Lokesh Vemani claimed silver, while Shaurya Ashwini and Godwin Anbkess won bronze. In the women’s events, Joys Ashita clinched gold in Foil, with teammate Kanaglakshmi winning silver. Prachi Lohan won gold in women’s Epee, while Nivedhya Nair and Anupriya secured bronze medals. In women’s Sabre, Jeferlin bagged gold, Aakhari won silver and Shreya Gupta took bronze. India will look to build on its strong opening-day performance in the remaining events of the championship.

national_raw_news.title: Hockey World Cup to be played in new format; quarterfinal stage scrapped 10 Aug 2026 | 6:16 PM 697
national_raw_news.content: The FIH Hockey Men’s and Women’s World Cup 2026 will feature a revamped competition structure, with the traditional quarterfinal stage scrapped and the top two teams from each of the two crossover pools advancing directly to the semi-finals. Belgium and the Netherlands jointly host the tournament from August 15 to 30. The new format means teams will have little margin for error from the outset, with results from the opening pool stage potentially carrying over into the next phase. India’s men have been drawn alongside England, Pakistan and Wales in Pool D, while the Indian women will face China, England and South Africa in their Pool D campaign. The tournament will begin with the 16 teams in each competition split across four pools of four. From August 15 to 20, every team will play three matches against the other sides in its pool, with the final standings determining the composition of the next phase. The top two teams from Pools A and D will move into Pool E, while the leading two teams from Pools B and C will form Pool F. The top two finishers from Pool E and Pool F will advance directly to the last four. The women’s tournament will conclude in the Netherlands on August 29, with the bronze-medal match followed by the final. The men’s World Cup will conclude in Belgium a day later, on August 30, with its bronze-medal match and final.

national_raw_news.title: India and Namibia decide to move bilateral trade beyond raw-material-based composition towards value addition 11 Aug 2026 | 9:38 PM 89
national_raw_news.content: The Fourth Session of the India-Namibia Joint Trade Committee (JTC) concluded in New Delhi today. The session which began yesterday, was led by Joint Secretary, Department of Commerce, Amit Kumar from the Indian side while the Namibian delegation was led by the Namibian Executive Director, Ministry of International Relations and Trade Ndiitah Nghipondoka-Robiati. The agreed minutes of the Session were signed by the two Co-Chairs today. The Ministry of Commerce and Industry said that during the meeting, both sides underlined the need to move bilateral trade beyond a raw-material-based composition towards value addition within Namibia, and to translate discussions into concrete mechanisms with defined timelines and assigned responsibilities. The Ministry added that the bilateral merchandise trade between India and Namibia rose to over 592 million dollars in 2025-26 from 568 million dollars in 2024-25.

national_raw_news.title: IT collection over eight lakh crore so far; 23.09% higher than last fiscal same period 11 Aug 2026 | 8:36 PM 64
national_raw_news.content: The Income Tax Department, as of the 10th of this month, has collected over 8.11 lakh crore rupees net direct tax for the financial year 2026-27 so far. It is 23.09 percent higher growth as compared to the financial year 2025-2026 during the same period. The collection includes corporate tax of over 2.70 lakh crore rupees and non-corporate tax of 5.07 lakh crore rupees. The department has also issued refunds of over one lakh 43 thousand crore rupees. The gross direct collection has recorded a significant growth of over 19 per cent, amounting to more than nine lakh 54 thousand crore rupees.

national_raw_news.title: RBI Governor asks banks to adopt AI with caution for accountability and customer trust 11 Aug 2026 | 7:15 PM 789
national_raw_news.content: The Reserve Bank of India Governor has called on Indian banks to adopt Artificial Intelligence with a clear focus on innovation, accountability and customer trust. Addressing the 2026 edition of FIBAC in Mumbai, the RBI Governor said AI could transform Indian banking by improving credit delivery, customer service, financial inclusion, operational efficiency and fraud detection. At the same time, the Governor cautioned banks about risks including opaque “black box” models, algorithmic bias, concentration of technology providers, data privacy, cyber vulnerabilities and excessive dependence on AI-driven decisions. The Governor urged banks to maintain an inventory of AI systems, establish board-approved AI governance policies, stress-test AI models and ensure meaningful human oversight. The Governor reiterated that the RBI chooses a principles-based and proportionate approach over a rigid, prescriptive one, as AI capabilities and risks will differ across large and small banks.

Minister of State for Information and Broadcasting and Parliamentary Affairs Dr. L. Murugan provided the information in response to a question raised by Dr. Alok Kumar Suman in the Lok Sabha on Wednesday . According to the Press Information Bureau (PIB), the Government has established a Fact Check Unit (FCU) within PIB to verify claims related to Central Government ministries, departments, PSUs and other government organisations. The verified information is disseminated through various platforms. Doordarshan and Akashvani also disseminate verified information through their news bulletins, programmes and digital platforms. DD News follows a multi-layered editorial process involving fact-checking, cross-verification through multiple credible sources and editorial scrutiny before broadcast. PIB Fact Check content is also regularly integrated into Doordarshan and Akashvani’s news and digital platforms to counter misinformation. The Government also highlighted the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021, notified under the Information Technology Act, 2000. The rules prescribe due-diligence requirements for intermediaries and a Code of Ethics for digital news publishers and OTT platforms. They also provide a three-tier grievance redressal mechanism involving publishers, self-regulating bodies and government oversight. The Government said it is supporting the film and media sector through initiatives including the Development, Communication and Dissemination of Filmic Content (DCDFC) Scheme, India Cine Hub and the National Film Heritage Mission. These initiatives cover areas such as film festivals, promotion of Indian cinema, shooting permissions, and preservation, restoration and digitisation of India’s cinematic heritage. On international media cooperation, the Government said Prasar Bharati maintains content-sharing arrangements and broadcasting agreements with organisations across the world. It has 48 active Memoranda of Understanding with broadcasters from different countries...
